derivation: Written by applying contract/semantics.md to the recorded frames by hand.
NOT generated by running any binding.
ts_str '2026-04/20-13:30:00' read as America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4 on that
date) gives 2026-04-20T17:30:00Z. The DLL's own ts_utc carries
5m/15m/30m/1h — the intraday grid runs from 09:30 ET. 17:30:00Z is
13:30 ET, which is 240 minutes after the 09:30 anchor; 240 divides by
5, 15, 30 and 60, so the instant is already a grid edge in all four.
1d — the daily grid anchors at 04:00 ET (§4). 13:30 ET is after 04:00,
publisher's timestamp is NOT the bucket: EL stamps a daily bar with
the chart's own Date/Time, and it is the binding that aligns.
notes: This fixture is the end-to-end coverage for wire v3's whole point — the
BarType/BarInterval → tf mapping in the DLL's wire_timeframe(). Before it
existed every recorded frame was tf '1m', so a regression in that table
(BarInterval 60 mapped to '60m', say) reached a binding with nothing in
CI to catch it, and a second binding had no sample to check against.
The QQQ frame comes from EL_PublishTickEx, the frozen legacy entry point.
It has no BarType/BarInterval parameters, so it can only ever have meant
1m — pinned here so the shim cannot drift.
THE TWO 1d FRAMES ARE NOT A DUPLICATE. They are BarInterval 0 and
BarInterval 1 on BarType 2, and they are identical on the wire on
purpose: a subscriber never sees BarType/BarInterval, so both readings of
'daily' have to arrive as the same tf. TradeStation 10 reports 0 — a live
SPY daily chart logged 'bar_type=2.00 bar_interval=0.00' and the DLL
refused it with -5 until this was fixed. 1 is what the ABI documented
before that measurement, and installs this repo cannot see still send it.
THREE FRAMES ARE ABSENT ON PURPOSE. The harness also called EL_PublishBar
with (bar_type=1, bar_interval=2), (bar_type=3, bar_interval=1) and
(bar_type=2, bar_interval=2). All three returned -5 and published nothing,
which is why this fixture has 7 lines and not 10. The DLL does not guess:
an unmappable interval filed under a default would put one interval's bars
in another's partition, and nothing downstream could tell. The 2-day case
is why BarType 2 stops at BarInterval 1 instead of accepting anything —
on that BarType the interval is a day multiplier. See error_codes.md.
seq is per-symbol (§6.1): SPY runs 1..6 across five different timeframes
on one topic, QQQ runs 1. Interval does not get its own counter — the
topic is the stream.
